character.appendages: Exactly two short clawed arms, two legs and one tail. No wings, horn, ears, second tail or floating ornament appears in any cell. The restrained cells add an external pale wrap across the torso that crosses the body and is never drawn as part of the skin.
character.contactAndOrigin: Shared source origin is [28, 41] on a [64, 64] canvas, from a native bounds union of [-16, -27, 24, 8]. Every cell is placed against that origin; no cell is recentred or resized.
character.faceAndExpression: The mouth is closed in neutral, walk and rest poses and opens wide with a red interior and a visible tooth row in the call, bite and hit poses. The eyes are dark with a single pale highlight and become occluded when the head turns away from the viewer. The same face is not repeated across poses: it compresses and turns with the head angle.
character.locomotion: Motion is a two-frame step cycle with the legs swapping, plus a head-down forward lunge, a low crouch, a wide prone lie, a back-arched call pose, a curled tumble and a flat defeat pose displaced along the ground. The tail swings with the body and the head leads every turn; the feet stay on the contact line except in the lifted and tumble frames.
character.morphology: Upright bipedal reptile. The head is close to a third of the body height and carries a wide jaw that opens to an upper and lower tooth row. Two short clawed arms sit high on the chest, two thick legs end in pale claws at the contact line, and a thick tail tapers behind the body and counterweights every lean.
character.restraint: Restrained cells are cell_027, cell_028, cell_029, cell_030, cell_032, cell_035, cell_036, cell_037, cell_039, cell_040, cell_041, cell_042. Each mirrors its unrestrained sequence tick for tick and needs an external wrap that crosses the body and is never read as anatomy.
character.specialStates: cell_044 is a warm flash state; cell_047 is a black silhouette state; cell_048 is a black silhouette state; cell_061 is a stone-gray state; cell_064 is a evolution white state. Each is derived by recolour from an authored pose, never redrawn.
